key_findings: Every public tool is one typed ToolContract carrying Zod input/output schemas, an audited ToolEffects record, mechanically derived MCP annotations, a returnsTargetContent flag and validated examples; catalog order never selects a handler (src/contracts/toolContractTypes.ts:36-66; AGENTS.md:39).

Effects are a closed ten-boolean vocabulary (mutatesTarget, mutatesSession, writesFilesystem, launchesProcess, accessesNetwork, changesUiState, mayDiscardData, executesForeignCode, mutatesDevice, idempotent) hand-audited for 235 tools; a missing audit throws at build; readOnly/destructive/idempotent/openWorld hints derive from it with no name heuristics (src/contracts/toolEffects.ts:1-30, 54-762, 765-832).

REA has no permission handshake: annotations are 'hints, not authorization controls' and confirmation UI is the MCP client's job; the maintainer integration gate 'is not a per-call confirmation requirement or a sandbox guarantee' (docs/mcp-contracts.md:1219-1224; CONTRIBUTING.md:225-226).

Tool-design rules: start from the analyst question, six task shapes, primitives over workflows, strict inputs with explicit target identity, declare effects truthfully, limits only for real constraints ('An assumed agent budget is insufficient justification'), recovery kept with the owning contract, coverage derived from examined records ('Missing coverage is unknown, not absence') (docs/tool-design.md:3-28, 151-176, 108-149, 392-406).

Lifecycle ownership is an invariant: ownership separate from validity/readiness, failed cleanup retains the owner for retry via cleanup_incomplete, cancellation carried through finalization, 'REA never kills a process it cannot prove it owns' (AGENTS.md:19-23; docs/tool-design.md:290-430; docs/mcp-contracts.md:1207-1209).

Verification ladder: real public CLI/MCP workflow > production-boundary integration > producer goldens > module tests; 'a scripted sequence tests that sequence, not an agent's ability to discover it'; real engines need their own verify:* lanes and ~22 real-*.yml CI workflows; 'A lane must not imply that a host or target is covered when it was skipped' (docs/testing.md:404-462; docs/testing-lanes.md:18-23; .github/workflows/).

Agent usability is measured with a real agent: scripts/verify-agent-experience.mjs installs the packaged skill into a disposable Codex HOME via public rea setup, runs data-defined scenarios, and scores JSONL transcripts on first-tool routing, repeated calls, canonical-schema input failures, ordered tool subsequences, Evidence citation and token usage (tests/evaluation/model-evals/CodexAgentEval.ts:137-245; AgentEvaluationReport.ts:24-42).

Closed known-answer rubrics require the agent's final answer to be a strict JSON claim manifest bound to Evidence IDs; the grader authenticates Evidence from the transcript, binds it to the exact artifact path/SHA-256, and fails fabricated values, extra claims and unrelated citations (tests/evaluation/model-evals/KnownAnswerEvaluation.ts:44-118, 262-340; tests/boundary/mcp/agentKnownAnswerMcp.test.ts:17-120).

Text heuristics are explicitly labeled as non-factual: 'These metrics can still accept fabricated prose and must not be read as factual assessments'; scenarios without a rubric stay not_assessed (docs/client-verification.md:582-590).

Performance order is agent tokens/context first, then analysis time, then CPU/memory; 'Count the whole task, including schemas, extra calls and retries'; mechanisms are summary-first results with retained parent_evidence_id, a 13,312-byte compact input-schema budget, REA_MCP_TOOL_FAMILIES scoping, and examples that never embed full Evidence (AGENTS.md:41-67; docs/mcp-contracts.md:1587-1591, 1630-1640, 1716-1757).

Target content is untrusted by default: only seven tools are audited into TARGET_CONTENT_FREE_TOOLS, every other result and error carries _meta.provenance.untrusted_content, and server instructions tell agents to report run/install/download/send requests as prompt injection (src/contracts/toolEffects.ts:788-816; src/server/toolResultEncoding.ts:29-30; docs/mcp-contracts.md:462-501).

Skills are subordinate to contracts: 'do not use a skill as the primary repair for a discoverability or contract defect'; the packaged skill (v59) is routing + recovery + epistemic guidance and tells the agent to trust the connected server's live catalog over the skill text (AGENTS.md:93-97; .agents/skills/reverse-engineer-anything/SKILL.md:27, 286-291, 398-407).

REA's only write-capable app-driving surface is agent environments: a write tool is served only when later recorded reads confirmed its effect without contradiction, each withheld write carries a reason and a next-recording hint, generated values are deterministic and data/reset restores state (docs/agent-environments.md:731-760, 183-199, 480-492).

Action-capable tools are batch declarative scenarios (browser/Electron/native-UI/process) or explicitly 'unrestricted' debugger consoles marked with every effect true; no per-step interactive desktop driving tool was found (docs/browser-scenario-contract.md:1-50; docs/native-investigation.md:1013-1032; src/contracts/toolEffects.ts:58-104, 596-606).

Governance is fail-closed for execution/injection/mutation capabilities with human-owned PR readiness that AI must not attest to, and a PR-template 'Expected effects' checklist mirroring the effects vocabulary (CONTRIBUTING.md:133-226; .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md).
extensibility_points: Single typed ToolContract per tool from which catalogs, docs, skill metadata, SDK registration and tests are all generated (src/contracts/toolContractTypes.ts; scripts/generate-mcp-tool-catalog.mjs; scripts/generate-skill-metadata.mjs).
Closed effects vocabulary with mechanical annotation derivation and a build-time failure on any unaudited tool (src/contracts/toolEffects.ts:765-832).
Untrusted-by-default content marking with an explicit audited allowlist so new tools cannot silently lose the marker (src/contracts/toolEffects.ts:788-816).

Static capability declarations separated from lazy runtime service bindings; one-shot CLI adapters import only the selected factory; six-step 'Extending a capability' recipe (docs/capability-composition.md:8-34, 77-91).
Shared Evidence-input contract (evidenceInputSchema / getEvidenceInputContract / resolveEvidenceRequest) so any tool accepts inline or retained Evidence uniformly (docs/tool-design.md:178-220).

Tool families as an orthogonal scoping axis; server instructions and guided prompts compose from the active scope so guidance never names a disabled tool (docs/mcp-contracts.md:1716-1757; src/server/serverInstructions.ts).
Curated runtime-settings registry with typed bounds, enforcement owner and application point; 'A registry entry must not advertise authority REA lacks' (docs/design/limits-and-recovery.md:351-378).
Provider-neutral public names with per-provider coverage reporting; upstream capability alone does not require a new tool (docs/tool-design.md:5-9, 66-73).

Agent-evaluation scenarios are data (prompt, expectedFirstTool, requiredToolSubsequence, rubric, approvedTools) over a schema-versioned report, so new tool families add scenarios not harness code (scripts/verify-agent-experience.mjs:174-284).

Executable architecture rules: oxlint rules tested under tests/evaluation/*Rule.test.ts, scripts/verify/architecture-guards.mjs, and scripts/ci/require-provider-tests.mjs requiring named lifecycle cases per provider.
Dated verification records and per-slice spec.md/verification.md pairs indexed per PR (docs/verification/, docs/specs/agent-environments/README.md).
relevance_to_control_plane: BORROW: the ToolContract + closed effects vocabulary + mechanical hint derivation + build failure on unaudited tools; it is the cheapest way to make every action's side effects declarable and queryable.

BORROW: untrusted-by-default provenance marking on anything read from a target (UI trees, window titles, clipboard) plus server instructions about prompt injection; hosts can then escalate approval for drive tools after target content was read (docs/mcp-contracts.md:497-501).

BORROW: the agent-environments write-gating pattern (serve a write only when read-back confirms it; withheld writes carry reason + hint) as the admission model for auto-discovered app actions, and as the shape of per-action result: before/after observation plus effect status confirmed/unconfirmed/contradicted/side-effect.

BORROW: the agent-eval harness shape (disposable client HOME, skill installed via public setup, per-tool preapproval, JSONL transcript scoring, negative-routing scenario, retained transcripts) and the closed-rubric idea with the oracle changed to resulting application state read through an independent channel with state reset per run.

BORROW: lifecycle ownership rules (target identity bound at attach and re-verified before each action; failed cleanup retains the owner; cancellation carried through finalization; never kill an unproven process) for persistent attach/drive sessions.
BORROW: token-first delivery (summary-first with retained parent IDs, compact schema profile, family scoping, no full-record examples) since a control plane's UI-tree observations will be large.
BORROW: fail-closed governance for mutation capabilities, the PR-template effects checklist, and the rule that skills carry judgment while contracts carry discoverability.
CHANGE: destructiveHint collapses to true for every drive tool because executesForeignCode implies destructive; replace with reversibility, blast radius, persistence and data-loss axes.

CHANGE: readOnlyHint is false whenever the session records Evidence; split 'read-only with respect to the target' from 'mutates control-plane session' so observe tools are not treated as actions by approval policies.

CHANGE: REA leaves per-call authorization to the MCP client; an action surface must own per-call policy (target allowlist, effect-class gating, escalation after untrusted content) because client approval support is uneven.
CHANGE: the eval gate's repeatedCallCount === 0 rule must be keyed by target state revision / effect status, since identical drive calls can be correct.

CHANGE: REA's batch declarative scenarios with 'state is left as-is; REA does not attempt to restore it' must become step-wise tools with explicit idempotency/step IDs for reconciliation after dropped connections, and an explicit undo/restore contract or an explicit statement that none exists.

AVOID: generic 'run anything' tools; REA ships unrestricted debugger consoles but labels them with every effect true and isolates their session owner; prefer typed verbs and gate any residual generic executor separately.
AVOID: relying on text heuristics (keyword cues, substring coverage) as correctness; REA itself says they can accept fabricated prose.

AVOID: npx @latest fallbacks for a tool that drives software; copy REA's pinning of the shipped package specifier in skills and plugin manifests and its rule to acquire packages from a trusted directory outside the target.
constraints_or_risks: Authorization scope: REA states that authorization to inspect does not authorize execution, interception or device changes, that possession of a file or a debugging endpoint does not establish permission for every operation, and that a local-only design or 'authorized use only' disclaimer does not establish containment (DISCLAIMER.md:42-52; CONTRIBUTING.md:175-177); an observe+drive control plane falls in the class REA requires an explicit maintainer scope decision for.

Scope boundary: REA excludes DRM/license/anti-cheat/access-control bypass and anti-instrumentation evasion from first-party code, plugins, bundled scripts, defaults and examples, and says moving a capability into a plugin does not exempt it (CONTRIBUTING.md:156-171); the control plane should carry the same written exclusions.

Supply chain: quick start and the skill fallback use npx rea-agents (incl. @latest), mitigated by pinned specifiers in shipped skills and plugin manifests, 'trusted directory outside the target project', setup that never installs unrelated software and shows its plan; Hopper download integrity is a SHA-1 corruption check, not a signature (README.md:79-92; SKILL.md:71-77; scripts/generate-skill-metadata.mjs:31; SECURITY.md:49).

Commercial-tool licensing: REA provides no IDA/Hopper/JEB license or entitlement and states an open-source bridge grants no additional user, machine, feature, automation, hosting or output-sharing rights; IDA access is read-only and attached GUI databases are never saved or closed (DISCLAIMER.md:80-86; AGENTS.md:9).

No sandbox: REA's security boundary is per-session capability tokens over current-user sockets; it does not protect against same-user malicious processes; Frida/GDB/Rizin tools can change memory, files, network and behavior and retire the active analysis session (SECURITY.md:25-49; references/runtime-observation.md:14-33).

Hand-maintained effects audit: TOOL_EFFECTS is a literal record enforced only by a missing-entry throw; whether declared effects are checked against observed behavior is unknown; auto-generated tools would need conservative default effects.
Heuristic metrics can accept fabricated prose; only closed rubrics assess facts, and several scenarios are not_assessed (docs/client-verification.md:582-590).
Real-agent evaluation runs only through Codex CLI; other clients have loopback-model lanes that do not prove live model behavior (docs/client-verification.md:46-60, 475-482).
Maintenance volume: ~2,500 lines of testing docs, 53 verification records and ~35 CI workflows; copying the structure without the volume is the realistic path.
